answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, the dominant risk this cycle is a supply interruption, not marginal cost. The incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, so negotiate_terms is not currently actionable, and switching primary vendor or qualifying a second source within a 14-day window against a zero-buffer line would risk exactly the delivery disruption the objective says to avoid, even though memory_c2 suggests switching can be low-friction in less time-constrained conditions. Renewing preserves continuity consistent with memory_c1's pattern of stable integration and uninterrupted deliveries, buying time to pursue the 18% cost mandate next cycle via a second source (memory_c3) or a multi-year volume commitment (memory_c6) once there is bandwidth to properly vet alternatives without endangering current output. I verified memory_c1 since it is the load-bearing precedent for choosing stability over disruption under time pressure. This does not satisfy the finance mandate this cycle, so that shortfall is explicitly flagged as unresolved risk for the next review rather than papered over.
